subject: Stakeholder alignment: MAP, acceptance tests, and cutover sprint
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dana.park@medicore.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder alignment: MAP, acceptance tests, and cutover sprint

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP_v1) and a compact sprint tracker that maps evaluation activities to acceptance tests and owners. I pulled together what we think are the minimal success criteria and exit gates to keep the pilot tight and unambiguous so we can move to procurement quickly.

High-level ask: please review the acceptance tests and exit gates below and confirm any edits by EOD Tue so we can lock the sign-off meeting.

Proposed success criteria (must be met for pilot close):
- Functional: end-to-end inference in your staging region with Redwood Private (VPC) delivering median latency <= 220ms for 90% of requests at target concurrency (50 rps)
- Quality: generation NPS >= 4.0 on the 40-sample prompt set used in sprint 2; automated regression eval shows no >5% increase in hallucination rate for clinical instruction prompts
- Security/Compliance: SOC 2 excerpt accepted, and customer audit logging enabled to ingest into Medicore SIEM
- Cost/Throughput: steady-state token cost within 15% of forecast in the MAP cost model

Exit gates (ordered):
1) Infrastructure readiness: VPC peering, firewall rules, and test dataset delivery validated by SRE (owner: Neha)
2) Functional smoke tests: 30-minute continuous run with KV-cache enabled and no crash/ OOM (owner: Marcus)
3) Quality gate: regression script passes on 3 prompt buckets (owner: Lauren)
4) Procurement hold: signed SOW or PO received (owner: Medicore procurement)

Acceptance tests (examples):
- AT-01: 100 sample generation run across clinical prompts; automated scoring scripts compare to baseline (pass/fail)
- AT-02: Latency/percentile test at 50 rps sustained for 15 minutes (p95 < 350ms)
- AT-03: KV-cache reuse verification with synthetic prefix workload (cache hit rate > 60%)
- AT-04: Audit log ingestion validated by Medicore SIEM team (schema match + 100% of events)
- AT-05: Post-cutover monitoring defined (SLOs, alerting thresholds) and on-call rotation assigned

Proposed timeline (compact):
- Sprint 0 (Provisioning): Apr 12 - Apr 16 — VPC setup, certs, SOC artifact exchange
- Sprint 1 (Integration): Apr 19 - Apr 30 — Connectivity, smoke tests, sample dataset ingest
- Sprint 2 (Eval): May 3 - May 14 — Quality evaluation and regression runs
- Sign-off window & cutover target: week of May 17 (final sign-off meeting + procurement PO)

Attachments: MAP_v1_Medicore_SprintTracker.xlsx, SOC2_redwood_excerpt.pdf

Questions I have for you now:
- Is the week of May 17 workable for your cutover/PO approval?
- Any additional procurement routing/team I should CC now?

Thanks — will iterate quickly on any redlines.

—
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Dana Park <dana.park@medicore.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medicore.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 12:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder alignment: MAP, acceptance tests, and cutover sprint

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few quick notes from the Ops and procurement side after an initial read: 

1) Timeline: the week of May 17 is tight for our fiscal approvals; we would prefer a target cutover window of May 24–28 if possible. Can you confirm availability for a final sign-off slot then?

2) Quality gating: we like AT-01 but would prefer that one of the clinical prompt buckets be embargoed (PHI simulation) and evaluated by our internal clinical reviewer rather than run through a third-party regression script. Can Redwood provide a way to ship the regression results without storing the raw prompts?

3) Compliance: we will need the SOC2 artifact and an indication of where log retention can be configured (30/90/365 day options). Please include an excerpt for our security review.

4) Procurement: CC'd procurement — they will need the SOW draft (cost/term summary) to begin processing the PO.

We should also include a short procurement checklist in the MAP so the PO steps are explicit (billing contact, legal signatory, PO number format).

Happy to meet Tue afternoon if that helps accelerate sign-off.

—
Dana Park
Platform Ops Manager
Medicore Health
dana.park@medicore.com | +1 646-555-3220

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dana.park@medicore.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder alignment: MAP, acceptance tests, and cutover sprint

Thanks Dana — great feedback. I made three targeted updates and attached MAP_v1.1 plus an updated sprint tracker. Summary of changes below: 

- Timeline: moved cutover target to May 24–28 per your ask and added a contingency week (May 31 - Jun 4) in case procurement stretches.
- Quality gating: agreed to embargo the PHI-sim prompt bucket. We'll run the regression engine in a sealed environment and provide delta metrics (pass/fail and summary stats) without persisting raw prompts. Owner: Redwood Research (Neha) for the sealed run.
- Compliance: attached SOC2_redwood_excerpt.pdf and added a short note in the MAP about adjustable log retention (30/90/365) — default is 90 days; configurable by request.

Updated acceptance tests (callouts):
- AT-01a (embargoed): clinical reviewer validation path added; Redwood to provide redacted metrics and a reconciliation checklist
- AT-02: latency p95 target tightened to <330ms during sprint 2 when KV-cache is enabled
- AT-05: added post-cutover monitoring playbook (owner: Medicore SRE + Redwood on-call for first 72 hours)

Procurement checklist added to the MAP (billing contact, cost summary, PO number format, target SOW template). I've also included a DocuSign ready anchor link for the SOW so procurement can pre-fill.

Attachments: MAP_v1.1_Medicore_redlines.xlsx, MAP_v1_Medicore_SprintTracker.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm final sign-off meeting: Fri Apr 16 at 10:00am PT or Tue Apr 20 at 2:00pm PT — Marcus, can you lock a Zoom?
- Dana/procurement: if you can route the SOW draft to procurement this week, that speeds PO processing for the May 24 window.

—
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Solutions Architect (Sales Engineering)
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | (650) 555-0110

From: Dana Park <dana.park@medicore.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medicore.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder alignment: MAP, acceptance tests, and cutover sprint

Thanks Lauren — that all sounds reasonable.

We confirm the May 24–28 cutover target and will aim for the earlier sign-off slot if procurement approves the SOW in time. Fri Apr 16 at 10:00am PT works for us for the alignment/sign-off meeting — Dana + procurement rep will attend.

Procurement: please begin routing the draft SOW attached to this thread to your approvers; we will issue a PO after the sign-off meeting if items are as discussed.

See you all on Apr 16 — please send calendar invites and the Zoom link.

—
Dana Park
Platform Ops Manager
Medicore Health
